summary: Iteration 14 — Deals moderation workflow + Ads system (sponsored advertisements) fully validated. 22/22 backend pytest passed. Frontend: /admin/deals, /admin/ads, /ads/new, /ads/mine, /deals all render correctly with the expected widgets (status tabs+counters, 4 stat tiles, full ad editor with 4 templates + 3 color pickers + 3 alignments + desktop/mobile preview toggle, sponsored ads section on /deals with 'Créer une publicité' button visible for company).

issues: CTR shown as 150% (3 clicks / 2 views * 100) which is mathematically correct but UX-unusual; consider capping displayed CTR at 100% or showing 'n/a' when clicks > views (test data artifact)

action_items: Optional UX: cap CTR display at 100% on /admin/ads when clicks > views (edge case from test data).

Optional: surface 'Mes publicités' as a direct link in the company avatar dropdown for discoverability (currently /ads/mine reachable via URL & via 'Créer une publicité' button on /deals, which is acceptable).
critical_code_review_comments: ads_routes.py _company_quota_ok counts {draft, pending, published, suspended} toward quota — drafts are intentionally allowed past quota via save_as_draft=True (verified), but a free company that already submitted a draft will see used=1/1 even though the draft is not 'active'. Consider excluding 'draft' from quota_used so /ads/mine quota.used reflects only diffused/awaiting ads.
ads_routes.py POST /ads has no input validation: an empty title is accepted (only Pydantic type-checks). Add a min_length=3 on AdIn.title + cta_url HttpUrl validation to harden.
ads_routes.py track_view/click endpoints are unauthenticated and accept anonymous POST — add IP-rate-limit (or hash of IP+ad_id+hour) to prevent click-bombing/inflated CTR.
ads_routes.py update_ad does NOT re-check quota when an author moves a draft to 'pending' via submit:true — a free company could pile drafts then mass-submit beyond quota.
server.py admin_list_deals counts loop runs 7 serial count_documents queries — acceptable but aggregatable to 1 $group for scale (same comment as iter13 for sources-status).

success_rate.frontend: 100% — all 5 pages render correctly with required widgets
